svg.aria-label: How the ESP32 controls the power switches (MOSFET gates)
svg.title: How the ESP32 controls the power switches (MOSFET gates)
svg.text: How the ESP32 switches the power: MOSFET gates explained
Six switches, one GPIO pin each. GPIO HIGH = switch ON, LOW = switch OFF.
A MOSFET is an electronic on/off switch for the
The GATE is its control input. A voltage between
gate and source closes the switch; 0 V opens it.
The gate draws almost no current, but an IRF3205
needs about 10 V to turn fully on. An ESP32 pin only
gives 3.3 V, so a gate driver (TC4427) converts
3.3 V logic into a 0 V / 12 V gate signal.
N-MOSFET IRF3205 between the load and ground
GPIO27 HIGH: gate 12 V, switch ON, load powered
GPIO27 LOW: gate 0 V, switch OFF, load off
10 kΩ pull-down: OFF while the ESP32 boots or if a wire
falls out. Same circuit on GPIO16, 17, 21 (LOAD2-4).
P-MOSFET in the + wire, turned on by a small 2N7000
HIGH: 2N7000 on, gate pulled to 0 V, ON
LOW: 1 kΩ holds gate at source voltage, OFF
D1 blocks the bus from back-feeding the buck.
Every ground (supply, buck, panel -, ESP32, sensors) must be joined for the sensors to work. A switch in a SOURCE's minus wire would be bypassed by that shared ground,
so sources are switched in their + wire (high-side). Loads can simply be switched between the load and ground (low-side).
4 · Soft-start: PWM on the SRC_SW gate (GPIO25, 20 kHz)
drawn far slower than real: 20 kHz = 20 000 pulses per second
All six pins start LOW at boot, so every switch is OFF.
On any fault the controller drives all six LOW.
E-stop (normally closed) cuts the drivers' 12 V,
so every gate drops to 0 V in hardware.
